table.name: atom
table.purpose: Atoms of molecules: one row per atom, linking each atom to its parent molecule and giving its chemical element symbol. IDs like TR031_31 suggest atom 31 of molecule TR031; t04 likely holds the molecules (referenced by col_002) and t03 references atoms from t01.

col_001.name: atom_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Unique atom identifier of the form <molecule_id>_<atom_number>, e.g. TR031_31 = atom 31 of molecule TR031. Referenced by t03.col_001 and t03.col_002.

col_002.name: molecule_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the parent molecule (e.g. TR031); the prefix of col_001. References t04.col_001, so t04 is the molecule table. 444 distinct molecules across 12333 atoms.

col_003.name: element_symbol
col_003.description: Chemical element symbol of the atom (h, c, o, n, cl, p, zn, br, si, ...). Organic-heavy distribution (H ~45%, C ~37%) consistent with molecular structures.

table.name: bond
table.purpose: Segment/leg-level detail table: each row is a segment of a route (t04), identified by a composite code combining the route code with two numbers (likely start/end points or segment indices). Referenced by t03 via col_003.

col_001.name: segment_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Composite code 'TRxxx_a_b': route code (col_002) plus two numbers, likely the segment's start and end identifiers (e.g., stop/node numbers or positions along the route).

col_002.name: route_id
col_002.description: Route code (e.g. TR031), referencing t04.col_001. Many segments per route.

table.name: connected
table.purpose: Edge/segment table linking pairs of nodes (e.g. track/trace points) from t01, with each row identified by a composite key in t02 combining the two node IDs. Likely a graph of connections between numbered points within each TR group (e.g. transitions between track segments).

col_001.name: from_node_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the first node of a pair; references t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Values like 'TR018_11' denote group TR018, node 11.

col_002.name: to_node_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the second node of a pair; references t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Same format as col_001, e.g. 'TR018_12'.

col_003.name: pair_id
col_003.description: Composite identifier of the node pair, formed by concatenating the two node IDs (e.g. 'TR018_11_12' = col_001 + '_' + node number of col_002); references t02.col_001 (many-to-one).

table.name: molecule
table.purpose: Unresolved. The table has only two columns: a unique identifier (col_001) and a binary sign flag (col_002). It is referenced by t01.col_002 and t02.col_002, suggesting it classifies entities from those tables into two categories, but the evidence is insufficient to determine what the entities or the two categories are. The 'TR' prefix of the identifiers hints at 'transaction', 'transfer', 'trial', or similar, but this is speculative.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of the table. A unique text identifier with a 'TR' prefix followed by a zero-padded number (e.g. TR000, TR477). It is referenced by t01.col_002 and t02.col_002, so each row represents an entity that rows in t01 and t02 point to. What the prefix stands for (possibly 'transaction', 'transfer', 'trial', etc.) cannot be determined from the data.
